'''Michael Struwe''' (born 6 October 1955 in [[Wuppertal]]) is a German mathematician who specializes in [[calculus of variations]] and [[nonlinear partial differential equation]]s. He won the 2012 [[Cantor medal]] from the [[Deutsche Mathematiker-Vereinigung]] for "outstanding achievements in the field of geometric analysis, calculus of variations and nonlinear partial differential equations".<ref name=ems>{{cite web|title=Cantor medal for Michael Struwe, von Kaven-prize for Eva Viehmann |url=http://www.euro-math-soc.eu/node/2938 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20131211121744/http://www.euro-math-soc.eu/node/2938 |url-status=dead |archive-date=11 December 2013 |work=European Mathematical Society |accessdate=11 December 2013 |year=2012 }}</ref>

He studied mathematics at the [[University of Bonn]], gaining his PhD in 1980 with the title ''Infinitely Many Solutions for Superlinear, Anticoercive Elliptic Boundary Value Problems without Oddness''.<ref>{{cite web|title=Michael Struwe|url=http://genealogy.math.uni-bielefeld.de/id.php?id=54337|work=Mathematical Genealogy Project|accessdate=10 December 2013}}</ref>  He took research positions in Paris and at [[ETH Zürich]] before gaining his [[habilitation]] in Bonn in 1984. Since 1986, he has been working at ETH Zürich, initially as an assistant professor, becoming a full professor in 1993.<ref name=ems/> His specialisms included nonlinear partial differential equations and calculus of variations.

He is joint editor of the journals ''Calculus of Variations'', ''[[Commentarii Mathematici Helvetici]]'', ''International Mathematical Research Notices'' and ''Mathematische Zeitschrift''.

His publications include the book ''Variational methods (Applications to nonlinear PDE and Hamiltonian systems)'' (Springer-Verlag, 1990), which was praised by [[Jürgen Jost]] as "very useful" with an "impressive range of often difficult examples".<ref name=jost>{{cite journal|last=Jost|first=Jürgen|title=Variational methods (Applications to nonlinear PDE and Hamiltonian systems)|journal=Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society|date=January 1993|volume=28|series=New series|issue=1|pages=149–153|authorlink=Jürgen Jost|doi=10.1090/s0273-0979-1993-00339-2|doi-access=free}}</ref>

Struwe was awarded a [[Gauss Lectureship|Gauss Lecture]] by the [[German Mathematical Society]] in 2011. In 2012, Struwe was selected as one of the inaugural fellows of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 19 January 2014.</ref>
